episode_title: You Don't Need Perfect Conditions to Start | The Purpose Rules: Mindset, Pt. 3
question: Why is waiting for perfect conditions to start financial change counterproductive?
transcript_excerpt: The perfect time never shows up because there is always another bill, another surprise, another reason to wait one more month. Staying stuck can become its own kind of addiction because the uncomfortable is familiar, and the alternative asks us to acknowledge where we really are, accept our circumstances, and work through them without knowing exactly how long it will take.

episode_title: You Don't Need Perfect Conditions to Start | The Purpose Rules: Mindset, Pt. 3
question: What are the five stages of the Purpose Rules framework for financial transformation?
transcript_excerpt: Stage one is your top three goals, not ten. Stage two is your budget, not a punishment but a map to find the holes in the boat. Stage three is your net worth, what you own minus what you owe. Stage four is protection through life insurance and living benefits. Stage five is the savings rule: aim to save 20 percent of what comes in, and at minimum 10 percent, and learn to live off the rest.

episode_title: You Don't Need Perfect Conditions to Start | The Purpose Rules: Mindset, Pt. 3
question: Why do most people stay stuck in financial desperation, and how can they begin to escape?
transcript_excerpt: People stay stuck because it is nearly impossible to get out of our own way; we need guidance, mentorship, and coaching. Getting out starts with self-awareness, where you stop pretending and accept the facts for what they are, then make a decision that you are willing to do some things differently. The first real step is asking for help, whether through a book, podcast, workshop, mastermind group, or coaching, because most people who try this without support end up falling backwards.

episode_title: You Don't Need Perfect Conditions to Start | The Purpose Rules: Mindset, Pt. 3
question: What are the five signs someone is living in quiet desperation regarding money?
transcript_excerpt: Sign one is avoiding looking at your numbers. Sign two is Sunday night dread becoming part of the week. Sign three is living in when-then thinking: when I get the raise, then I will deal with it. Sign four is spending to feel better and then feeling worse. Sign five is stopping planning anything fun.

episode_title: You Don't Need Perfect Conditions to Start | The Purpose Rules: Mindset, Pt. 3
question: How can identifying inherited money beliefs help someone break free from financial limitation?
transcript_excerpt: Most inherited money beliefs, called money monsters, are beliefs running in the background of every money decision and come from what was seen and heard growing up. Once you put a name to one, it loses about half its power. The exercise is to write down three money beliefs, where each came from, and mark each one keep or release, because your past does not deserve your eternal loyalty.
